articles.title: Dry-Roasted Poha Chivda: A Low-Oil Diwali Snack That Stays Crisp for Weeks
articles.excerpt: Thin poha dry-roasted until crisp, then tossed with nuts and a mustard-seed tempering in just 3 tablespoons of oil — a complete sourced recipe for festive snacking without deep frying.
articles.nri_angle: A make-ahead, shippable Diwali savoury for diaspora kitchens: one batch covers guests, gift jars and the tea tin, and keeps crisp for up to two weeks airtight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Add thin poha in a wide pan. Dry roast on low flame till it is crisp. Keep it aside.
In the same pan heat oil. Add peanuts and roast till crisp.
Add cashew, roasted gram dal, dry coconut slices and roast for 3-4 minutes.
Then add raisin and roast till the raisins puff up. Keep the nuts aside.
In the same pan add mustard seeds and let it crackle.
Add green chili, curry leaves and saute till crisp and dry. Then add hing, turmeric, red chili powder, roasted nuts and mix well.
Now add nuts mixture to roasted poha along with salt, powdered sugar, aamchur powder and mix everything well.
Cool completely before storing; store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

articles.title: Diwali 2026 Recipes: Nine Traditional Dishes and the Kaju Sweets to Make at Home
articles.excerpt: From chakli and bhakarwadi to rasmalai and kaju katli, NDTV Food's festive lists — plus a full cashew katli recipe — for Diwali on Sunday, November 8.
articles.image_caption: Kaju katli, the cashew sweet at the centre of the Diwali recipe collection.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families can make the full faral and mithai spread at home ahead of Diwali on November 8, with dry snacks keeping one to two weeks in airtight jars.

steps: Grind cashews in a dry blender to a fine powder. Sieve to remove any coarse pieces. Do not over-grind or the fat will release and make it oily.
In a heavy pan, combine sugar and water. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook to a one-string consistency.
Reduce heat to very low. Add cashew powder, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook for 6-8 minutes until the mixture comes together as a soft dough and leaves the sides of the pan.
Add cardamom powder. Turn off heat.
Transfer to a greased surface. Cool until warm enough to handle. Knead gently for 1-2 minutes.
Roll out to 3-4mm thickness using a rolling pin. Apply silver vark if desired.
Cut into diamond shapes using a sharp knife. Cool completely before removing. Store in an airtight box.
